raised: Fees and returns are nearly the same across companies, so the choice feels like picking from a near-tie and leaves the reader unsure
In option ב, the cheapest first row (Infinity flexible index) looks like the best pick but isn't S&P, which nearly misled the reader
The top title and bullets are written for the designers, not for the user
The other product buttons aren't explained; the reader doesn't know what they are
There are too many 'במה הכסף מושקע' buttons, with unclear terms (הלכה, אג"ח ממשלתי סחיר, כספי, כללי)
The reader doesn't understand how 'מניות' (active) differs from 'עוקב מדדי מניות'
The orange 'בציור בלבד… עוד 13 קבוצות' line is just a list of names and adds nothing
Option ב mixes every type in one list, so the reader must read small tags to find S&P; cheapest-first pulls the eye to unwanted tracks
Unclear whether 'מהחיסכון' and 'מההפקדות' are two separate fees that are both paid
The exposure figures (מט"ח 97% vs 100%) are not understood
The reader doesn't know what the 5-digit 'קופה' number is
Unclear why well-known companies show 'פחות מ־3 שנים' returns
'לפני דמי ניהול ולפני מס' leaves the actual return unclear
Unclear what the '>' at the end of each row opens
No translation of the fee percentages into shekels (e.g. per ₪10,000)
No information on how to join or whether there's a minimum amount
No information on switching track or company later, or what it costs
No information on tax or when money can be withdrawn
No comparison of a kupat gemel with buying an S&P fund through a bank or app

problems.why: The reader's near-tie remark is about the tracks' numbers being almost the same, not about the lists failing to convey anything about the companies themselves, so no raised item matches the person's problem.
